names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 1 Νοεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Καισάριος, Δάσιος, και άλλοι πέντε Μάρτυρες, Σάββας, Σαβινιανός, Αγρίππας, Αδριανός και Θωμάς το νήπιο», with the rank words left off.
Read out of the title on his name link behind the line for 1 ноября ст. ст., «Кесарий Дамасский, мч.», with the rank word left off. The day's own line declines it as «Кесария».

feast.note: His name page lists this day and no other.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 1 ноября ст. ст. — «Мчч. Кесария , Дасия и с ними пяти (VII).»

attestations.note: The line's «Мч.» is martyr, which this folder already held. It names two of the seven and counts the other five without naming them, so the five the Greek page names take no Russian row: a row resting on a count is not a row resting on a reading. The name link gives him the by-name «Кесарий Дамасский», of Damascus, which this folder's English form already carried from the Greek. The calendar serves no life page for the company.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Καισάριος, Δάσιος, και άλλοι πέντε Μάρτυρες, Σάββας, Σαβινιανός, Αγρίππας, Αδριανός και Θωμάς το νήπιο»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 1 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The entry enumerates all seven of its members, each with his own heading, so it is seven folders. The page's one epigram names only this man, «Σὺν ἓξ συνάθλοις… Τέμνουσι Καισάριον», which is why the other six take their English forms from his name. The corpus's three other Caesariuses — the brother of Gregory the Theologian, the companion of Julian, and one kept by date on 20 April — are none of them this man. No year, so no `dates` object; Damascus is where they were taken and is written into the English form, and no location is recorded. No hymn. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (1 October 2026).

death.note: The first date this folder has held. days.pravoslavie.ru closes the company's line «(VII)», the seventh century; neither doxologia.ro nor saint.gr dated the seven at all, and the Greek notice this folder was written from gives no emperor and no reign.
